were fabricated using arc melting furnace using high purity elements (99.95 %) under a pure Ar atmosphere. The alloy ingots were re-melted at least five times to obtain homogeneous chemical composition.
The ingots were then drop-casted into a copper mold with a dimension of 5 x 12 × 50 mm3.
Then the produced ingots were subsequently hot-rolled at 1150 ◦C with a of 65 % thickness reduction to reduce casting defects.

After hot rolling, homogenization treatment was carried out at 1200 ◦C for 1h, followed by aging treatment at 1000 ◦C for 1h to form homogenous distribution of precipitates. After each heat treatment stage, water quenching was performed.

which show the presence of randomly oriented grains and annealing twins (ATs), implying that the matrix possesses low stacking fault energy (SFE).
